_note: Every assumption of the economy model. Edit any 'value' to change the model; no code changes are needed. 'kind' is 'data' (from a cited source), 'derived' (arithmetic on cited data, method stated) or 'assumption' (the drafter's judgement, to be revisited). Sources point to research/12-economy.md and research/13-leaving-the-eu.md, where the full citations are. Units: € (= IR£ after exit, at par) billions at current prices; people in thousands; shares as fractions.

baseline._about: Ireland in 2025 (the model's year 0). These figures reproduce the real economy at the start; the model is calibrated so that year 0 matches them.

household_consumption.label: Household consumption, excluding VAT and excise
household_consumption.source: CSO ISQ01 individual consumption €154.42bn (2025) less VAT €22.94bn and excise €6.47bn (EFO Table 11); research 12 §2.3, §3.1

household_energy_imports.label: Imported energy bought directly by households
household_energy_imports.source: About 30% of the €7.49bn energy import bill (CSO TSA06 2025): residential oil, gas and coal plus private road fuel, from the shares of final consumption in SEAI's 2024 energy balance (research 12 §6.1). The 30% split is the drafter's estimate

medicine_imports.label: Medicines for domestic use paid in foreign currency
medicine_imports.source: The State's medicines bill, 'almost €3 billion' (Department of Health projection for 2024, research 12 §4.3). Treating all of it as imported is an assumption

gov_consumption.label: Public services: pay plus goods and services
gov_consumption.source: CSO GFA01 2025: compensation of employees €36.14bn + use of goods and services €21.34bn

public_investment.label: Public investment (gross)
public_investment.source: CSO GFA01 2025: net acquisition of non-financial assets €9.52bn + depreciation €7.76bn

private_investment.label: Private investment (modified)
private_investment.source: Modified GFCF €73.20bn (CSO NAQ05, 2025) less public investment €17.28bn

transfers.label: Social and other transfers, subsidies
transfers.source: CSO GFA01 2025: social benefits €43.39bn + other current transfers €4.11bn + subsidies €3.55bn + capital transfers €5.06bn, less the net EU contribution below

eu_net_contribution.label: Net contribution to the EU budget
eu_net_contribution.source: About €800m in 2024 (MEP's estimate; no official figure found; research 13 §5)

other_revenue.label: Other revenue (capital taxes, property, fees, sales, investment income, one-offs)
other_revenue.source: General government revenue €145.05bn (CSO GFA01 2025) less labour taxes, consumption taxes and corporation tax as defined here

domestic_exports.label: Exports of Irish-owned firms
domestic_exports.source: Enterprise Ireland client exports €38.86bn (2025) + tourism receipts €7.0bn (CSO BPA19); research 12 §2.4. The CSO's wider figure for domestic firms' services exports (€73bn, 2023) is not used; see the economy-model spec

mne_purchases.label: Multinationals' purchases of Irish services and materials

mne_taxes.label: Corporation tax paid by foreign-owned multinationals

mne_employment.label: Employment in foreign-owned agency client firms

domestic_wages.label: Wages in the domestic economy
domestic_wages.source: Compensation of employees €165.16bn (CSO NAQ08 2025) less multinationals' payroll €26.0bn

domestic_va.label: Value added of the domestic economy
domestic_va.source: GNI* less multinationals' payroll and corporation tax, less VAT and excise (which the model records as household taxes): 333.97 − 26.0 − 28.8 − 29.41

gni_other.label: Other items in GNI* not modelled
gni_other.source: Zero by construction: domestic value added is defined as the remainder

hours_per_worker.label: Average hours per worker (index, today = 1)
hours_per_worker.source: An index, so no figure is needed

state_funds.label: State funds: Future Ireland Fund, ICNF, ISIF

fx_reserves.label: Existing official reserves usable on exit day
fx_reserves.source: Not sourced (the ECB data portal could not be reached). Set to zero so that only the TARGET settlement counts: a deliberately cautious assumption

target_claim.label: Central Bank's TARGET claim on the Eurosystem

household_deposits.label: Household deposits in Irish banks
household_deposits.source: Not sourced in this pass; an order-of-magnitude figure used only to size capital flight. Owner should replace with the Central Bank's money and banking statistics

farm_income.label: Value added of agriculture, forestry and fishing
farm_income.source: CSO NA016, 2025 (research 12 §2.1); used as the farm income the Art. 67 guarantee protects

cap_eu_funding.label: EU-funded CAP payments
cap_eu_funding.source: Nearly €7.5bn from the EU budget over 2023–27 (European Commission; research 13 §5) ÷ 5

household_disposable_income.label: Household gross disposable income
household_disposable_income.source: CSO ISQ01, 2025 (research 12 §2.3); used to calibrate the share of the domestic surplus households receive

ca_star.label: Modified current account (CA*)
ca_star.source: CSO BPA39, 2025 (research 12 §2.4); the model is calibrated to it

design._about: How the republic is run, and how the economy is assumed to respond. Policy choices follow the constitution; behavioural parameters cite evidence where it exists.

horizon.label: Years modelled
horizon.source: Transition (years 0–10) plus ten years to a long-run position

exit_year.label: Year the republic leaves the EU and the euro

transition_years.label: Years over which the transition is phased

provision_years.label: Years to build up public provision

trend_growth.label: Underlying real growth of the domestic economy
trend_growth.source: Drafter's assumption, below the 2.2% real growth of non-multinational sectors in 2025 (research 12 §2.1) to allow for the shocks of the transition

labour_force_growth.label: Growth of the labour force
labour_force_growth.source: Drafter's assumption (ageing slows labour-force growth; research 12 §3.5)

productivity_growth.label: Underlying productivity growth
productivity_growth.source: Trend growth less labour-force growth, so that unemployment is stable with no shocks

inflation_target.label: Central Bank inflation target
inflation_target.source: Set by the Assembly under Art. 61.2; 2% is the drafter's placeholder

indexation.label: Share of last year's inflation passed into this year's wages and domestic prices
indexation.source: Drafter's assumption: partial indexation, so a currency shock raises prices for several years without spiralling

export_elasticity.label: Response of export volumes to a cheaper currency
export_elasticity.source: Drafter's assumption, at the low end of trade-elasticity estimates; Irish-owned exports are heavily food, whose markets are constrained by tariffs and quotas

wto_loss_agrifood.label: Fall in agri-food exports on WTO terms with both the EU and the UK
wto_loss_agrifood.source: Copenhagen Economics' WTO scenario: beef exports −35%, dairy −40% (research 13 §4.2), applied to the 72% of agri-food exports sold to the EU and UK

wto_loss_other.label: Fall in other Irish-owned exports on WTO terms
wto_loss_other.source: Copenhagen Economics: exports 7.7% below baseline by 2030 in the WTO scenario (research 13 §4.2). An analogy from Brexit, not a forecast

herd_export_share.label: Beef and dairy share of agri-food exports
herd_export_share.source: (€3.4bn beef + €7.3bn dairy) ÷ €19bn, Bord Bia 2025 (research 13 §4.1). Exports are assumed to fall in proportion to the herd

farm_guarantee_share.label: Share of lost farm income replaced
farm_guarantee_share.source: Art. 67.2: income no lower than the previous five-year average

cap_replacement.label: Share of EU farm payments the State replaces after exit
cap_replacement.source: Drafter's assumption: the republic keeps farm support whole

provision_expansion.label: Extra public provision: childcare, the Care Service, transport, the energy allowance
provision_expansion.source: Drafter's assumption for Arts. 21, 24, 68, 71; to be costed item by item

public_investment_push.label: Extra public investment: housing, retrofits, grid, rail

private_investment_fall.label: Fall in private investment over the transition
private_investment_fall.source: Drafter's assumption: conversion to social ownership (Art. 47.2) and uncertainty; Przeworski and Wallerstein find investment falls while redistribution is anticipated (research 12 §8.1)

public_capital_return.label: Productivity gain from extra productive public investment
public_capital_return.source: Drafter's assumption, in the range commonly reported for the output elasticity of public capital; not separately sourced in this pass

investment_waste_max.label: Share of public investment wasted when no one takes part in planning
investment_waste_max.source: Drafter's assumption representing Kornai's 'investment hunger' (research 12 §8.4). Waste falls in proportion to participation. The weakest-evidenced link in the model

hours_offset.label: Share of an hours cut recovered by higher output per hour
hours_offset.source: Drafter's assumption; four-day-week trials report output largely maintained, but they are small and self-selected

energy_import_cut.label: Share of imported energy replaced by domestic renewables by year 10
energy_import_cut.source: Drafter's assumption; 64.9% of indigenous energy was already renewable in 2025 and imports are 92.8% fossil (research 12 §4.1)

jg_wage.unit: € bn per thousand people a year
jg_wage.label: Job Guarantee wage (about €30,000 a year)
jg_wage.source: Drafter's assumption, near a full-time living wage

jg_capacity.label: Most the Job Guarantee can absorb
jg_capacity.source: Drafter's assumption: organisational capacity, built up over the first years

jg_build_years.label: Years to build the Job Guarantee to capacity

t_w.label: Tax and PRSI on labour income
t_w.source: (Income tax incl. USC €36.58bn + social contributions €24.61bn) ÷ compensation of employees €165.16bn, 2025

t_s.label: Tax on the domestic surplus
t_s.source: Domestic corporation tax (€32.9bn underlying less €28.8bn paid by foreign multinationals) ÷ domestic operating surplus (€249.77bn − €139.16bn)

m_i.label: Import content of investment
m_i.source: Drafter's assumption: machinery (€17.1bn of modified investment) is mostly imported, construction (€43bn) mostly domestic (research 12 §2.5)

m_x.label: Import content of Irish-owned exports
m_x.source: Drafter's assumption: feed, fertiliser and fuel in food exports (research 12 §4.2)

social_ownership_share.label: Share of the domestic surplus earned by socially owned enterprise by year 10
social_ownership_share.source: Drafter's assumption for Art. 47 (public, municipal and co-operative)

public_dividend_share.label: Share of socially owned enterprises' after-tax surplus paid to the State
public_dividend_share.source: Drafter's assumption; co-operative reserves are indivisible (Art. 50.3), so most surplus is reinvested

interest_rate.label: Effective interest rate on public debt today

foreign_law_debt_share.label: Share of public debt under foreign law, which stays in euro
foreign_law_debt_share.source: Unverified: new bonds are under Irish law, some older programmes under English law (research 13 §2.1). 20% is the drafter's placeholder

domestic_debt_held_at_home.label: Share of domestic-law debt held by residents
domestic_debt_held_at_home.source: Drafter's assumption; interest on the rest is paid abroad

domestic_absorption.label: Share of private net saving that savers will lend to the State
domestic_absorption.source: Drafter's assumption; under capital controls Iceland's trapped savings financed the budget (research 12 §7.4)

cb_ceiling.label: Ceiling on Central Bank lending to the State
cb_ceiling.source: Voted each year under Art. 61.4; 3% is the drafter's placeholder

credibility_premium.unit: inflation points per point of GNI*
credibility_premium.label: Extra inflation from Central Bank financing
credibility_premium.source: Drafter's assumption representing the critics' expectations channel (Mankiw, Blanchard, IMF staff; research 12 §8.3). Set to 0 for the pure MMT view

swf_return.label: Return on the Social Wealth Fund
swf_return.source: Drafter's assumption, close to Norway's 3% expected real return plus inflation (research 12 §8.2)

swf_draw_rule.label: Most of the Fund that may be spent on investment in a year
swf_draw_rule.source: Drafter's assumption, after the Future Ireland Fund's 3% cap (research 12 §3.3)

windfall_share.label: Share of multinational corporation tax that is windfall
windfall_share.source: €16.8bn 'potentially transitory' ÷ €28.8bn (Department of Finance; research 12 §3.2). Ring-fenced in the Fund before exit (Art. 60)

target_settled.label: Share of the TARGET claim settled in foreign currency on exit

mne_departure_start.label: Year multinationals start to leave
mne_departure_start.source: Drafter's assumption: once notice is given

deposit_rate.label: Interest on household deposits (not modelled)
deposit_rate.source: Interest reaches households through domestic holdings of public debt instead

interest_rate_rise.label: Rise in the effective interest rate over the transition
interest_rate_rise.source: The Department of Finance projects 2.7% by 2030 inside the euro (EFO); a new currency and capital controls are assumed to add a little more. Drafter's assumption

foreign_rate_premium.label: Extra interest on debt that stays in euro
foreign_rate_premium.source: Drafter's assumption: a risk premium once the State has redenominated its own-law debt

tax_increase.label: Extra progressive income and wealth tax, phased in over five years
tax_increase.source: Drafter's assumption. Tax is already about 39% of GNI* (research 12 §8.1); this takes it towards Danish levels. Set to 0 to see the design without new taxes

import_elasticity.label: Response of import volumes to dearer imports
import_elasticity.source: Drafter's assumption at the low end of usual estimates: Ireland's essential imports (energy, food inputs, medicines) are hard to substitute in the short run

breaks._about: Where the model says the economy breaks. Each threshold is a judgement, stated openly.

budget_gap.label: Unfinanced deficit that counts as a break
budget_gap.source: Any gap above 0.5% of GNI* after savers and the Central Bank ceiling

reserve_months.label: Reserves below this many months of essential imports
reserve_months.source: The traditional three-months-of-imports rule of thumb for reserve adequacy, applied here to essential imports only (energy, food, medicines)

inflation.label: Inflation counted as a break
inflation.source: Drafter's threshold; Chile's inflation passed 260% in 1972 (research 12 §7.4), Iceland's peaked at 18.6%

interest_share.label: Interest taking more than this share of revenue
interest_share.source: Drafter's threshold; interest was 2.0% of revenue in 2025 (NTMA)

mne_exit.label: Share of multinationals that leave
mne_exit.range_source: No forecast exists. Leaving the EU removes their main reason to be here; the charter regime (Art. 52) is meant to keep some. Full range shown (research 12 §7.3)

capital_flight.label: Deposits that leave during the notice period
capital_flight.range_source: Greek deposits fell about 23% in a few months of 2015 (research 12 §7.4)

devaluation.label: Fall of the punt on exit day
devaluation.range_source: Sterling −15% (1992); Nomura's Irish break-up estimate about −30% (2011); Iceland's króna −50% or more (2008) (research 13 §2.3)

trade_terms.label: Trade terms with the EU and UK (0 = tariff-free deals, 1 = WTO terms with both)
trade_terms.range_source: The UK–EU agreement (zero tariffs) at one end; EU and UK most-favoured-nation tariffs at the other (research 13 §4.2–4.3)

herd_reduction.label: Reduction in the herd by year 10
herd_reduction.range_source: From no change to a 60% reduction; agriculture is 38.7% of emissions with 6.9 million cattle (research 12 §4.2, §6.2)

hours_reduction.label: Cut in average working hours by year 10
hours_reduction.range_source: From no change to a four-day week (−20%)

energy_price.label: Change in world energy prices
energy_price.range_source: Ireland's energy import bill rose from €6.2bn in 2021 to €13.1bn in 2022 (CSO TSA06), +111%

participation.label: Share of residents who take part in local assemblies and planning
participation.range_source: From marginal involvement to mass participation. Kerala devolved 35–40% of its plan budget to village assemblies; Porto Alegre's budget was later starved (research 06 §5, §9). The effect on investment waste is the drafter's assumption
